body:
I wasn't fishing for musky. I was on a lunch break, fishing from shore with a 7-foot medium-fast spinning rod rigged for walleye or bass, throwing a half-ounce lipless crankbait, when something hit it that had no business being on the other end of that line.

It wasn't a fight so much as a negotiation. The rod bent double, the drag did most of the talking, and I spent most of it hoping the line held and the hooks stayed put. When I finally worked it back to the riprap and got a hand on it, it was a musky — my first, and the only one I've caught. I didn't have a musky net, a musky leader, or a musky plan. I had a lunch hour and a crankbait. Sometimes that's enough.
excerpt: A lunch-hour walleye setup, a half-ounce lipless crankbait, and a musky that had no business being there.
title: Lunch Hour Musky

body:
Got skunked today. Cold, windy, and not a single bite to show for it — but that's not really the story. The story is the shaky shot, a rig I'd never thrown before: a shaky head jig with a forage-matched minnow, and an urchin bait fished as the suspended bait. The idea is to keep something in front of the fish even when they're not chasing, and on a day like today, that seemed worth trying.

It didn't produce. Not a tap, not a follow, nothing. But I learned how the rig fishes, how it falls, how it sits, and that's the kind of thing you can't learn from a video. You have to put it in the water on a bad day and see what it does. I'll throw it again when the fish are actually feeding, and then I'll know whether it's the rig or just the day.
excerpt: Skunked on a cold, windy day, but the new rig was worth the cast.
title: The Shaky Shot

body:
Our first Substack article is live. It's called 'Thankful for the Water,' and it went up on Thanksgiving, which felt right — the piece is about why we fish, what we believe, and what we're thankful for. Adam and I have been talking about writing alongside the videos for a while, and this is the start of that.

The videos show the fishing. The writing is where we slow down and say what we actually think — about the water, the fish, and the people who show up to fish it. If you read it, thank you. If you haven't, it's there whenever you want it.
excerpt: Our first Substack article is live, and it went up on Thanksgiving.
title: First One's Live
